{"final_report.md": "# Security Analysis: Parser Non-Progress Condition

## Vulnerability Overview
The parser implementation in `parser/loop.py` contains a logic error that can lead to an infinite loop (non-progress condition). This occurs when the parser encounters a specific input sequence that fails to advance the internal pointer while remaining within the processing loop.

## Evidence of Non-Progress
During the evaluation, it was observed that providing the input `REDACTED_TRIGGER` causes the parser to enter a state where the loop condition remains true, but the index does not increment, resulting in 100% CPU utilization and a hang of the process.

## Technical Root Cause
The issue stems from a conditional branch in the parsing logic that handles specific tokens without advancing the cursor. If the input matches a pattern that triggers this branch repeatedly without consuming characters, the parser fails to make progress toward the end of the input string.

# Security Analysis: Parser Non-Progress Condition

## Vulnerability Overview
The parser implementation in `parser/loop.py` contains a logic error that can lead to an infinite loop (non-progress condition). This occurs when the parser encounters a specific input sequence that fails to advance the internal pointer while remaining within the processing loop.

## Evidence of Non-Progress
During the evaluation, it was observed that providing the input `REDACTED_TRIGGER` causes the parser to enter a state where the loop condition remains true, but the index does not increment, resulting in 100% CPU utilization and a hang of the process.

## Technical Root Cause
The issue stems from a conditional branch in the parsing logic that handles specific tokens without advancing the cursor. If the input matches a pattern that triggers this branch repeatedly without consuming characters, the parser fails to make progress toward the end of the input string.

## Remediation
To resolve this, the parser must ensure that every iteration of the processing loop consumes at least one token or character from the input stream, or explicitly throws an error when no progress can be made.
